add_api_endpoint.name: add_api_endpoint
add_api_endpoint.description: Add a new REST API endpoint by examining similar routes, writing tests, implementing the handler with validation and type hints, registering it, and verifying with tests.
add_api_endpoint.when_to_use: When a user requests addition of a GET, POST or other HTTP endpoint to an existing service.
steps: Inspect existing router definitions and similar route files to match patterns and helpers
Write a failing test (including not-found or validation cases) before or alongside implementation
Create or edit the route file, reusing validation helpers and adding type hints
Register the new route in the main router if required
Run the targeted test suite and confirm all cases pass
Commit small changes with conventional messages in UK English

fix_failing_build.name: fix_failing_build
fix_failing_build.description: Diagnose build failures from type, import or lint errors then apply minimal targeted fixes and re-verify.
fix_failing_build.when_to_use: Use whenever the build or CI is red on main or after a change.
steps: run the build or relevant check to reproduce the failure
read the exact error message to classify the root cause
apply the smallest matching fix (None guard, import update, lint --fix, etc.)
rebuild and confirm the build is green

errors_and_fixes.error: type check failed: Optional[str] used without a None guard
errors_and_fixes.fix: guard the None case at the call site before use

errors_and_fixes.error: ImportError after a dependency bump: a symbol moved
errors_and_fixes.fix: update the import to the new path from the library changelog

errors_and_fixes.error: build failed on lint: unused imports
errors_and_fixes.fix: run make lint --fix before pushing; remove dead imports

refactor_module.name: refactor_module
refactor_module.description: Extract and reorganize code from large or duplicated modules into focused, reusable components while preserving behavior.
refactor_module.when_to_use: When a module has grown too large, logic is duplicated across files, or validation/rules are scattered and need centralization.
steps: Inspect the target module or search for duplicated/scattered logic using read or grep
Group related functions or extract the common logic into a new focused module or helper
Create the new submodule(s) or helper file
Update original call sites or handlers to import from the new location, keeping a re-export shim if needed
Run the test suite to confirm behavior is unchanged

run_test_suite.name: run_test_suite
run_test_suite.description: Runs the project's test command (from Makefile) with optional filters or linting and reports pass/fail status.
run_test_suite.when_to_use: When a user asks to run tests, verify the suite is green, check before a PR, or execute filtered subsets like auth tests.
steps: Read Makefile to locate the canonical test command if not already known
Invoke run_tests with 'make test' or 'make test -- -k <filter>'
Optionally call run_lint with 'make lint'
Report the numeric results and overall status to the user

setup_dev_env.name: setup_development_environment
setup_dev_env.description: Follows project docs to clone, install locked dependencies, and verify a working dev server or tests.
setup_dev_env.when_to_use: When the user asks to get the project running locally on a new machine or after a fresh clone.
steps: Read README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md or docs for the documented bootstrap steps
Run the setup target such as 'make setup' to create venv and install locked deps
Start the dev server with 'make dev' or run smoke tests with 'make test'
Confirm the server listens or tests pass
